### J-1 The logged entry header drops the word `Asked`, which the grill's resume rule depends on
- quote: "under an entry header that keeps the ID (`## Q7 · J-7 · <date>`)"
- quote: "a lint on `## Asked` entries comes only if agents still drift"
- situation (consistency): a grill session starts on a spec whose `grill.md` ends with a `## Q7 · J-7 · <date>` entry that has no `Answer:` line. The approved grill FR-20 says the session must resume "asking first any `Asked` entry that has no answer", and this header does not match that. The entry is either skipped or the question is asked twice. The spec's own non-goal refers to `## Asked` entries, so the two parts of the spec disagree on what the header is. Either the spec must keep `Asked` in the header, or it must raise a change request against grill FR-19 and FR-20 and update the resume step in the grill skill.
- fix: keep an `Asked` marker in the header (for example `## Asked · Q7 · J-7 · <date>`), or add a change request against grill FR-19, FR-20 and AC-21 and make the non-goal's wording match.
- validation: confirmed: FR-13 and AC-10 set the header to `## Q7 · J-7 · <date>`, but `skills/grill/SKILL.md` line 64 writes `## Asked · Q7 · <ID> · <date>` and line 29 resumes from "an `Asked` entry with no answer" (grill FR-19/FR-20). The spec's own non-goal and Risks still say `## Asked` entries, and nothing in the spec settles which header wins.
- disposition: spec-fix by agent: FR-13/AC-10: the shown message is logged in the existing ## Asked · Q7 · <ID> entry before showing; resume rule unchanged

### J-2 Facts' sources move from the question body to `Refs:`, against an approved grill requirement
- quote: "facts in plain words, sources in `Refs:`"
- quote: "the step no longer asks for facts naming their source in the question body"
- situation (consistency): the approved grill FR-4 says each question shows "the verified facts it rests on, each with its source (an RF-n, a file:line or a spec ID)". Under this spec the question shows the facts without their sources, and the sources appear only at the foot of the message. A human reading the question can no longer match a given fact to its source. The spec does not raise a change request against grill FR-4, and AC-17 tests the removal as if it were the goal.
- situation (consistency): The approved grill spec (`.nio/specs/grill/spec.md`, FR-4 and the 2026-10-25 decision "every fact in a question carries its source") requires each fact in a question to carry its source in the question. After this change a question shows, say, "the export takes 3 days" and "the limit is 500 rows" in the body, with RF-4 and file:line in a `Refs:` line at the bottom. The human can no longer see which source backs which fact. The spec rewrites the grill's step 6 on purpose, but it names no grill FR-4 change and no change request exists, and the memory rule requires a change request first.
- fix: state in the spec that it changes grill FR-4 and add the change request, or keep each fact's source in the body and put only the IDs in `Refs:`.
- validation: confirmed: Approved grill FR-4 and AC-4 require each fact "with its source" in the question. The plain-talk spec moves sources to `Refs:` (FR-17, AC-17), and no decision or change request names grill FR-4. The decisions list does flag the "at most 3 lines" change, but not this one.
- disposition: spec-fix by grill: FR-17/AC-17: each fact names its source beside it in plain words; IDs and file:line in Refs; grill FR-4 holds

### J-3 `nio jury answers` does not keep working unchanged with the labelled lines
- quote: "so `nio jury answers` keeps working unchanged"
- quote: "`Question:` holding the shown question line, then `Context:`, `Options:` and `Refs:`"
- situation (consistency): `src/nio/jury.py`, `answers()`, reads the options with `^Options[^:]*: (.*(?:\n(?!Answer:|Patched:).*)*)`, which keeps every line after `Options:` up to `Answer:` or `Patched:`. With the FR-13 order, the `Refs:` line falls inside that span and is appended to the last option's label. If the human answers "3" to an entry whose option 3 is "Ship it" with `Refs: J-7 · FR-10, FR-11 · jury.py:268`, the extracted answer becomes "Ship it Refs: J-7 · FR-10, FR-11 · jury.py:268 [human]". So the extraction no longer matches what the human chose, and AC-23 fails for numbered answers.
- situation (logic): FR-13 orders an entry as `Question:`, `Context:`, `Options:`, `Refs:`, then the answer. In `src/nio/jury.py` (`answers`, line 204), the options capture is `^Options[^:]*: (.*(?:\n(?!Answer:|Patched:).*)*)`. It stops only at `Answer:` or `Patched:`, so the new `Refs: J-7 · FR-10, FR-11 · jury.py:268` line is swallowed into the last option's text. If the human picked the last option by number (for example "3"), the extracted answer becomes "<option text> Refs: J-7 · ...". That is not one-for-one with the entry. The decision says the parser is unchanged, and FR-15 says CLI output is unchanged, so no one is assigned to fix this. Context lines are also never in the parser's view, but they sit before `Options:` and are harmless.
- situation (consistency): FR-13 orders the entry as Question, Context, Options, Refs, then Answer. `answers()` in `src/nio/jury.py:204` reads Options up to the next `Answer:` or `Patched:` line, so the Refs line joins the last option's text. Take an entry `Options: 1. Keep (recommended) 2. Drop 3. Defer`, then `Refs: J-7 · FR-10`, then `Answer: 3 [human]`. `answers()` returns `Defer Refs: J-7 · FR-10` as the human's answer, not `Defer`. AC-23 ("extracts every human answer ... match the entries one for one") then fails for that case, and the Decisions claim that the parser keeps working unchanged is false.
- situation (consistency): The grill logs `Options: 1. Keep it (recommended) 2. Drop it`, then `Refs: J-7 · FR-10, FR-11 · jury.py:268`, then `Answer: 1 [human]`. jury.py's `answers()` regex for options (line 204) runs until the next `Answer:` or `Patched:` line, so the `Refs:` text is absorbed into the last option. A human who picks option 2 gets back `Drop it Refs: J-7 · FR-10, FR-11 · jury.py:268` as the answer that the scope lens reads. The spec's AC-23 check would fail on that entry.
- fix: name the change to `answers()` in the spec (stop the options span at `Refs:`), or move `Refs:` after `Answer:`, and add a test that a numbered answer comes back without the `Refs:` text.
- validation: confirmed: `src/nio/jury.py` line 204 captures options with `^Options[^:]*: (.*(?:\n(?!Answer:|Patched:).*)*)`, which stops only at `Answer:` or `Patched:`. Under FR-13's order the `Refs:` line lands inside that span and is appended to the last option's label. So the Decisions claim "keeps working unchanged" is false for a numbered pick of the last option.
- disposition: spec-fix by agent: FR-13: Refs: lives only in the ## Asked entry; the answer entry keeps Question/Options/Answer/Patched as today; AC-23 adds a last-option pick with no Refs in the answer

### J-5 A round gives one message several `Refs:` lines, against the definition of the Refs line, and the round's opening line is never logged
- quote: "**Refs line**: the last line of a message, holding the IDs, files, commands and sources the message rests on."
- quote: "three `Refs:` lines, one per question"
- situation (logic): the grill asks a round of 3 questions. AC-25 treats it as one message with one opening line and three `Refs:` lines. The Key entities definition (and FR-5, "end it with a `Refs:` line") allows exactly one `Refs:` line, as the last line. Also, FR-13 logs "what the human saw word for word", but only one entry per question is logged, so the round's first line ("Answer 5 questions, by number") appears in no entry. Under FR-24 the host question tool shows the first line and context in the question text, so the human saw that line but the log has no place for it.
- fix: define a round as N messages plus an opening line. State where the opening line is logged, or say it is not logged.
- disposition: spec-fix by agent: FR-25 and Key entities: a round is one message per question under an opening line; each question ends with its own Refs; the opening line is not logged

### J-6 A command shown in the body can carry an ID or slug, which the no-ID rule forbids
- quote: "WHEN the human must run a command THE SYSTEM SHALL show that command in the message body, not only in `Refs:`."
- quote: "no message shows an ID above its `Refs:` line"
- situation (logic): AC-4 requires the command "above the `Refs:` line". A command the human must run can take a slug or other ID as an argument, for example `nio check spec plain-talk` or a command that names a finding. The command is then an ID above `Refs:`, so SC-2 fails, and FR-3 ("never by an ID") fails, even though FR-23 was followed. The rules do not say which one wins.
- fix: say that a command shown for copying is exempt from FR-3 and SC-2, or that the command is shown without IDs.
- disposition: spec-fix by agent: FR-3, SC-2: a command shown for the human to copy is quoted exactly, IDs included

### J-7 "area" in the first line breaks the rule against NIO terms the human does not start by name
- quote: "only stage names (spec, grill, jury, plan) may be used as they are"
- quote: "the first line asks to pick or add an area"
- situation (logic): remember finds no memory area that fits a record. AC-21 requires a first line asking the human to "pick or add an area", and its `Refs:` lists `memory.areas`. "Area" is a NIO memory term, not a stage name, and FR-3 allows only the four stage names as they are. Following AC-21 literally breaks FR-3, and following FR-3 means AC-21's first line cannot say "area". The same tension applies to the terms `challenged` and `conflict` in FR-21 if they are shown to the human.
- fix: either add "area" to the allowed terms, or reword AC-21 to describe an area by what it does ("pick where this should be filed, or add a new place").
- disposition: spec-fix by agent: AC-21: ask where to file the record or add a new place, without the word area

### J-10 One bundle where the spec could be split into slices
- quote: "a shared block in each skill that talks to the human carries it, and a small test keeps the copies identical."
- quote: "**Independent test:** read each listed step in the five skills; each says what the human is asked in plain words,"
- situation (scope): one change touches NORTH_STAR, CLAUDE.md, five skills (about 20 places, per Q6) and a drift test. The drift test (US-3) and the per-skill rewrites (US-4) each have their own independent test, so they could ship as separate slices. A problem in one rewrite would hold up SC-3 for the whole change, and `epic: ""` in the front matter records that no split was considered. The grill chose one bundle (Q6), and Q9 says a long list "signals the spec should be split", so this is for the human to decide.
- fix: ask the human once whether to keep one change or split it into an epic with a drift-test slice and a rewrite slice; if one change, no edit is needed.
- disposition: out-of-scope by human: Keep one change: the block, the test and the rewrites land together so no skill is ever half-converted; mostly wording, low risk.

### J-13 The behaviour-change split in FR-7 has no testable criterion, and its stated misuse has no AC
- quote: "THE SYSTEM SHALL show in plain words every item that changes what the product does, however many, then one line counting the rest"

### J-15 Length and "plain words" are left to the human, with no number or sample

No change request against grill FR-4 is cited, so a grill question that follows FR-17 breaks the approved requirement. The spec's Decision line "This keeps the grill's rule that every fact carries its source" is the claim the text does not support.
- fix: either write a change request against grill FR-4 and AC-4 (the human decides whether the source is shown as an ID or only in `Refs:`), or keep the ID beside the fact and change only the wording around it.
- validation: merged: same as J-2

### J-21 The behaviour-change test in FR-7 is narrower than the grill's bar it cites
- quote: "what data is kept, or what it costs"
- situation (consistency): FR-7 says an item "changes behaviour when it passes the grill's bar", then restates the bar. The grill's step 4 in `/home/work/nio/skills/grill/SKILL.md` lists "what data is kept or changed". A change that alters existing data without changing what is kept, for example a backfill, passes the grill's bar but fails FR-7's restatement. Under UJ-2 it would be counted as "nothing you'd notice".
- fix: copy the grill's five items word for word into FR-7, or write "the grill's bar" only and drop the restatement.
- disposition: spec-fix by agent: FR-7: copies the grill's bar word for word (data kept or changed)

### J-22 A round's questions need a "what's needed" first line and are also forbidden one
- quote: "THE SYSTEM SHALL make its first line say what is needed from the human"
- quote: "as one message per question under that opening line"
- quote: "only the round's first line says what's needed"
- situation (logic): The grill is in rounds mode and asks 3 questions. FR-25 makes each question "one message", and FR-1 says every message's first line says what is needed ("Pick one"). AC-25 and FR-25 say only the round's opening line says it, and the opening line is not logged. So question 2's first line must both say "Pick one" and not say it. FR-13's `Question:` line (the shown question line) and AC-1's rule that the first line starts with `Pick one:` have no defined content for a question inside a round.
- situation (testability): FR-25 makes each question "one message per question", and FR-1 says every message's first line says what is needed. AC-25 says only the round's first line does. A test following AC-25 fails a compliant round, where question 2 starts "Pick one", or passes a round with no per-question first line. The Observable also never checks that the opening line is absent from `grill.md`, so a logged opening line passes.
- fix: Say that a question inside a round is exempt from FR-1's first-line rule, and say what its logged `Question:` line holds. Or drop "only" from AC-25 so that each question opens with its own need.
- validation: confirmed: FR-25 makes each question "one message", so FR-1 requires each message's first line to say what is needed. AC-25 and Q3 say that only the round's opening line says it and that questions in a round don't start with "Pick one:". Nothing in the spec exempts round questions from FR-1, and nothing says what the logged `Question:` line holds for them.
- disposition: spec-fix by agent: FR-25: a question inside a round has no first line of its own (the opening line meets FR-1); its Question: line holds the numbered question; AC-25 checks this and that the opening line is not logged

### J-23 The question tool's text cannot match the logged entry word for word
- quote: "THE SYSTEM SHALL put the first line, the context and the `Refs:` line in the question text, and each option's consequence in its description"
- quote: "then `Context:`, `Options:` and `Refs:`"
- quote: "and the logged entry matches it word for word"
- situation (logic): The grill asks J-7 through Claude Code's question tool. Under FR-24 the shown question text is the first line, the context and `Refs:`, and the options sit in separate option fields. FR-13 logs `Question:`, `Context:`, `Options:` and `Refs:` in that order, with `Options:` before `Refs:`. AC-24 requires the logged entry to match the question text word for word, but the log holds an `Options:` block that the question text does not, and in a different order. FR-13 also says "show exactly that text", which cannot hold when the text is split across tool fields.
- fix: State how the tool's fields map onto the logged lines. For example, the match is per field (question text to `Question:`, `Context:` and `Refs:`; option labels and descriptions to `Options:`), or the match covers the whole shown message rather than the question text alone.
- validation: confirmed: FR-24 puts the first line, context and `Refs:` in the question text and the option consequences in the option descriptions. FR-13 logs `Question:`, `Context:`, `Options:` and `Refs:` in that order, and AC-24 requires the logged entry to match the question text word for word. The log therefore holds an `Options:` block the question text lacks, in a different order. The spec never says how the tool's fields map onto the logged lines.
- disposition: spec-fix by agent: FR-13, AC-24: through a question tool the match is field by field (question text to Question/Context/Refs, options to Options)

### J-24 "Machine-checked" contradicts the non-goal of having no linter
- quote: "Only IDs, severity names and the word"
- quote: "Code that lints messages: enforcement is the instructions plus the self-check"
- situation (logic): FR-3 says IDs, severity names and "lens" are "machine-checked". The non-goals rule out any code that lints messages, and the only code is the drift test, which compares the blocks. So nothing machine-checks these words. AC-6 lists `blocker`, `major` and `minor` as words that must not appear above `Refs:`. A literal check would flag ordinary prose such as "a minor change", and there is no checker to apply it.
- situation (scope): an implementer reads FR-3 and builds a check that flags IDs or "lens" in messages. That is the lint the non-goal forbids. Another reader takes the non-goal at its word and writes no check, so FR-3's "machine-checked" claim is never met. The spec gives no check that would make the claim true.
- fix: Reword FR-3 to say these are the only terms a reader or test script can check mechanically, and that the human judges the rest. Or drop "machine-checked" and say who checks AC-6 and SC-2.
- validation: confirmed: The refuter's J-26 verdict, which it marked same-as J-24: FR-3 says IDs, severity names and "lens" are "machine-checked", but the Non-goals rule out code that lints messages, and the drift test checks none of those words. No check exists that could make the FR-3 claim true.
- disposition: spec-fix by agent: FR-3: no code checks messages; IDs, severity names and lens are what a transcript reader looks for (SC-2)

### J-25 Showing every behaviour change "however many" can break the glance-length rule
- quote: "however many"
- quote: "none is too long to take in at a glance"
- situation (logic): A jury approval has 30 dispositions and 12 of them pass the grill's behaviour bar. FR-7 requires all 12 in the body in plain words. AC-2 and FR-2 require that the human can take each message in at a glance. A 12-item body fails AC-2, and trimming it to meet AC-2 breaks FR-7. The spec does not say which rule wins.
- fix: Say that AC-2 and FR-2 govern the context only and that a list may run as long as its behaviour changes. Or add a threshold above which the list is grouped or split across messages.
- disposition: spec-fix by agent: FR-2: the about-3-lines limit is on context only; an FR-7 list runs as long as its behaviour changes (the human's Q9)

### J-26 FR-3 says messages are machine-checked, but the non-goals rule out a message lint
- quote: "Only IDs, severity names and the word "lens" are machine-checked; other terms are judged by the human (SC-1)."
- quote: "Code that lints messages: enforcement is the instructions plus the self-check; a lint on `## Asked` entries comes only if agents still drift."
- quote: "Only instructions enforce the shape, so agents may still put IDs in the body; the fallback is a lint on `## Asked` entries."
- situation (scope): an implementer reads FR-3 and builds a check that flags IDs or "lens" in messages. That is the lint the non-goal forbids. Another reader takes the non-goal at its word and writes no check, so FR-3's "machine-checked" claim is never met. The spec gives no check that would make the claim true.
- fix: reword FR-3 so it says only instructions and the self-check enforce the rule, with the human judging terms (SC-1). Or, if a machine check is wanted, have the grill decide it and remove the non-goal.
- validation: merged: same as J-24
